question: Question linked to image No. 19 A 77-year-old man found at home with right hemiplegia and global aphasia. Last seen asymptomatic 20 hours before. Cranial CT shown. Point out the CORRECT answer:

options.opa: The image does not allow to determine the time of ischemia; it could have been only a few minutes since the deficit appeared.
options.opb: Does not meet criteria for the administration of fibrinolytic treatment.
options.opc: Admission to a stroke unit is not indicated in this patient.
options.opd: Given the size of the infarction, a decompressive craniectomy should be considered before cerebral edema appears.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Right hemiplegia and global aphasia -> suggests a left hemisphere stroke -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Last seen asymptomatic 20 hours before -> indicates a time window for symptom onset -> 70% confidence. CHAIN: Cranial CT findings show a large infarction -> indicates significant brain tissue damage -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Right hemiplegia and global aphasia -> contralateral to the affected hemisphere -> 80%
analysis: The patient presented with right hemiplegia and global aphasia, suggestive of a large vessel occlusion causing a major stroke. The CT scan shows a large infarction involving a significant portion of the brain. Given the time frame of 20 hours since the patient was last asymptomatic, the ischemic injury is likely well-established. Fibrinolytic treatment is contraindicated beyond the time window for acute stroke management. Admission to a stroke unit is crucial for specialized care and monitoring. Considering the size of the infarction and the risk of cerebral edema, a decompressive craniectomy may be considered in selected cases to prevent herniation and further brain damage.
